sec.salah.title: Salah, Sunnah & Dhikr
sec.salah.note: Whoever attends Isha in congregation has the reward of standing half the night. And whoever prays Isha and Fajr in congregation has the reward of standing the entire night.
sec.quran.title: Quran — Understand & Implement
sec.quran.note: Fasting and the Quran will intercede for a servant on the Day of Resurrection.
sec.character.title: Intention, Heart & Character
sec.character.note: Actions are judged by intentions, and every person will get what they intended.
sec.charity.title: Charity & Service
sec.charity.note: The Prophet was the most generous of people, and he was most generous in Ramadan.
sec.lastTen.title: Last Ten Nights — Seek Laylatul Qadr
sec.lastTen.note: "Seek Laylatul Qadr in the odd nights of the last ten days." It could be any of the last ten nights — strive every single night.
sec.avoidance.title: Daily Avoidance Check
sec.avoidance.note: Whoever does not give up false speech and acting upon it, Allah has no need of him giving up his food and drink.
sec.abuBakr.title: Abu Bakr Challenge
sec.abuBakr.note: The Prophet asked four questions. Abu Bakr answered "I did" to all. The Prophet said: "Whoever combines these will enter Jannah."

hadith.1: Whoever fasts Ramadan out of faith and seeking reward, his previous sins will be forgiven.
hadith.2: When Ramadan begins, the gates of Paradise are opened and the gates of Hell are closed.
hadith.3: Fasting is a shield; so when one of you is fasting, let him not speak obscenely or act ignorantly.
hadith.4: There is a gate in Paradise called Ar-Rayyan, through which only those who fast will enter.
hadith.5: Whoever gives iftar to a fasting person will have the same reward without reducing theirs.
hadith.6: The supplication of the fasting person is not rejected.
hadith.7: Fasting and the Quran will intercede for the servant on the Day of Resurrection.
hadith.8: Every action of the son of Adam is for him except fasting, for it is for Me and I shall reward it.
hadith.9: Whoever does not give up false speech, Allah has no need of him giving up food and drink.
hadith.10: Seek Laylatul Qadr in the odd nights of the last ten days of Ramadan.
hadith.11: The best charity is that given in Ramadan.
hadith.12: Whoever stands in prayer on Laylatul Qadr out of faith, his past sins will be forgiven.
hadith.13: The Prophet was the most generous in Ramadan when Jibreel would meet him.
hadith.14: Ramadan is the month of patience, and patience is rewarded with Paradise.
hadith.15: When the last ten days began, the Prophet would tighten his waist belt and pray all night.
hadith.16: There is nothing equivalent to fasting.
hadith.17: The breath of a fasting person is sweeter to Allah than the scent of musk.
hadith.18: Whoever prays qiyam in Ramadan with faith and seeking reward will be forgiven.
hadith.19: Make dua to Allah with certainty that He will answer.
hadith.20: The strong is not the one who overcomes people, but who controls himself when angry.
hadith.21: Laylatul Qadr is better than a thousand months.
hadith.22: Whoever draws near to Allah with good character is like one who fasts and prays all night.
hadith.23: Allahumma innaka 'afuwwun tuhibbul 'afwa fa'fu 'anni — O Allah, You are Pardoning…
hadith.24: The one who recites Quran skillfully is with the noble scribes (angels).
hadith.25: Allah extends His hand at night to accept repentance of those who sinned by day.
hadith.26: Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day, let him speak good or remain silent.
hadith.27: Nothing is heavier on the Scale than good character.
hadith.28: The best of you are those who are best to their families.
hadith.30: Whoever fasts Ramadan then follows it with six days of Shawwal, it is as if he fasted forever.

tf.tf001.q: Whoever fasts Ramadan out of faith and seeking reward will have their previous sins forgiven.
tf.tf001.x: The Prophet ﷺ promised forgiveness of past sins for fasting Ramadan with faith and hope of reward.
tf.tf002.q: The special gate of Paradise reserved for those who fast is called Al-Firdaus.
tf.tf002.x: The gate is called Ar-Rayyan — only those who fast will enter through it.
tf.tf003.q: When Ramadan begins, the gates of Paradise are opened and the gates of Hell are closed.
tf.tf003.x: A month where every door to good is opened wide — make the most of it.
tf.tf004.q: Whoever gives iftar to a fasting person receives half of that person's reward.
tf.tf004.x: They receive the SAME reward — without reducing the fasting person's reward at all.
tf.tf005.q: The Prophet ﷺ described fasting as a shield.
tf.tf005.x: Fasting shields you — so the fasting person should not speak obscenely or act ignorantly.
tf.tf006.q: The dua of a fasting person can be rejected like anyone else's.
tf.tf006.x: The supplication of the fasting person is not rejected — especially at the time of iftar.
tf.tf007.q: Allah says every deed of the son of Adam is for himself, except fasting — which is for Allah, and He Himself will reward it.
tf.tf007.x: Fasting has a special, unlimited reward known only to Allah.
tf.tf008.q: If you keep up false speech while fasting, Allah has no need of you giving up your food and drink.
tf.tf008.x: Fasting is not just from food — lying and false speech strip the fast of its spiritual reward.
tf.tf009.q: If someone insults you while fasting, the Sunnah is to respond with a sharper insult.
tf.tf009.x: The Sunnah is to say: 'I am fasting' — and walk away from the argument.
tf.tf010.q: The breath of a fasting person is sweeter to Allah than the scent of musk.
tf.tf010.x: What seems unpleasant to people is beloved to Allah when it comes from worship.
tf.tf011.q: Fasting six days of Shawwal after Ramadan is like fasting the entire year.
tf.tf011.x: Ramadan (×10 reward) plus six days of Shawwal completes the reward of a full year of fasting.
tf.tf012.q: The Sunnah guideline for eating is one-third food, one-third drink, and one-third air.
tf.tf012.x: The Prophet ﷺ warned against overfilling the stomach — a lesson especially relevant at iftar.
tf.tf013.q: Praying Isha and Fajr in congregation carries the reward of standing the entire night in prayer.
tf.tf013.x: Isha in congregation = half the night; adding Fajr in congregation = the whole night.
tf.tf014.q: The two Sunnah rakahs before Fajr are better than the world and everything in it.
tf.tf014.x: Two short rakahs outweigh the entire dunya — never skip them.
tf.tf015.q: Whoever prays qiyam (night prayer) in Ramadan with faith and seeking reward will be forgiven their past sins.
tf.tf015.x: This is the promise behind Tarawih and night prayer in Ramadan.
tf.tf016.q: Witr prayer must always be exactly five rakahs.
tf.tf016.x: Witr can be prayed as 1 or 3 rakahs — make it your last prayer of the night.
tf.tf017.q: The Prophet ﷺ sought forgiveness (istighfar) more than 70 times every day.
tf.tf017.x: If the forgiven Prophet ﷺ did istighfar daily, how much more do we need it?
tf.tf018.q: Sending one salawat upon the Prophet ﷺ brings ten blessings from Allah.
tf.tf018.x: Every single salawat is multiplied ten times over.
tf.tf019.q: Allah descends in the FIRST third of the night asking: 'Who calls upon Me that I may answer?'
tf.tf019.x: It is the LAST third of the night — the most blessed time for dua and tahajjud.
tf.tf020.q: Duha prayer counts as charity for every joint in your body.
tf.tf020.x: A short mid-morning prayer that pays the daily sadaqah owed by your 360 joints.
tf.tf021.q: Praying twelve Sunnah rakahs daily earns you a house in Jannah.
tf.tf021.x: The regular Sunnah prayers around the five obligatory ones build you a home in Paradise.
tf.tf022.q: The night adhkar before sleep include Ayatul Kursi and the last two ayat of Surah al-Baqarah.
tf.tf022.x: Prophetic protection through the night until you wake.
tf.tf023.q: The Prophet ﷺ enjoyed long conversations after Isha.
tf.tf023.x: He disliked talking after Isha — sleep early and protect your Fajr.
tf.tf024.q: The most beloved deeds to Allah are grand one-time gestures rather than small consistent ones.
tf.tf024.x: The most beloved deeds to Allah are the most CONSISTENT, even if small.
tf.tf025.q: The Quran was revealed in the month of Ramadan as guidance for mankind.
tf.tf025.x: That is why Ramadan is called the month of the Quran.
tf.tf026.q: On the Day of Resurrection, fasting and the Quran will both intercede for the servant.
tf.tf026.x: Two companions of Ramadan standing up for you when you need them most.
tf.tf027.q: The one who recites the Quran skillfully will be with the noble scribes (angels).
tf.tf027.x: And the one who struggles while reciting receives DOUBLE reward — so keep reading either way.
tf.tf028.q: The standard mushaf of the Quran has 604 pages.
tf.tf028.x: That's why this app tracks 604 pages — about 20 pages a day completes it in 30 days.
tf.tf029.q: The Prophet ﷺ said: 'The best of you are those who learn the Quran and teach it.'
tf.tf029.x: Memorising even one new ayah puts you on this path.
tf.tf030.q: When the Quran is recited, we are commanded to listen attentively and be silent so we may receive mercy.
tf.tf030.x: Even listening to recitation is a rewarded act of worship.
tf.tf031.q: Tadabbur means reciting the Quran as fast as possible.
tf.tf031.x: Tadabbur is deep REFLECTION on the meaning — pondering transforms the heart and guides action.
tf.tf032.q: Jibreel would review the Quran with the Prophet ﷺ every Ramadan.
tf.tf032.x: And in his final year, they reviewed it twice — revise your Quran in Ramadan.
tf.tf033.q: The Quran is divided into 40 juz.
tf.tf033.x: The Quran has 30 juz — reading one juz a day completes it exactly in Ramadan.
tf.tf034.q: The Quran criticises those who command others to righteousness while forgetting themselves.
tf.tf034.x: Knowledge without action is incomplete — apply a lesson from today's reading.
tf.tf035.q: Actions are judged by intentions, and every person will get what they intended.
tf.tf035.x: The very first hadith of Sahih al-Bukhari — every deed takes its value from the heart.
tf.tf036.q: The strong person is the one who defeats others in wrestling.
tf.tf036.x: The strong is the one who CONTROLS HIMSELF when angry.
tf.tf037.q: Nothing is heavier on the Scale on the Day of Judgment than good character.
tf.tf037.x: Gentleness and good character outweigh mountains of other deeds.
tf.tf038.q: The Quran compares backbiting to eating the flesh of your dead brother.
tf.tf038.x: Would one of you like to eat the flesh of his dead brother? You would detest it.
tf.tf039.q: Riya (showing off) only slightly reduces a deed's reward — the deed still counts.
tf.tf039.x: Deeds done for show are REJECTED entirely. Riya quietly voids reward.
tf.tf040.q: When you make dua for someone in their absence, an angel says: 'Amin, and for you the same.'
tf.tf040.x: The fastest way to get your own dua answered — pray for your brother or sister first.
tf.tf041.q: Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day should speak good or remain silent.
tf.tf041.x: Guarding the tongue is half of good character.
tf.tf042.q: Humbling yourself for Allah's sake lowers your status among people.
tf.tf042.x: Whoever humbles himself for Allah, Allah will RAISE him.
tf.tf043.q: The best of you are those who are best to their families.
tf.tf043.x: Character starts at home — with the people who see you every day.
tf.tf044.q: Good character can bring the same reward as one who fasts all day and prays all night.
tf.tf044.x: A believer reaches the rank of the constant worshipper through good character alone.
tf.tf045.q: Allah extends His hand at night to accept the repentance of those who sinned during the day.
tf.tf045.x: And by day for those who sinned at night — the door of tawbah never closes.
tf.tf046.q: The Prophet ﷺ was at his most generous during Ramadan.
tf.tf046.x: He was the most generous of people — and even more so in Ramadan when Jibreel met him.
tf.tf047.x: Charity does NOT decrease wealth — Allah replaces and blesses what you give.
tf.tf048.q: The best charity is that given in Ramadan.
tf.tf048.x: Every deed is multiplied in this month — including your sadaqah.
tf.tf049.q: Whoever visits a sick person remains in the 'harvest of Paradise.'
tf.tf049.x: A visit, a call, or even a supportive message counts.
tf.tf050.q: In the famous hadith of the four questions, it was Umar (RA) who answered 'I did' to all four.
tf.tf050.x: It was ABU BAKR (RA) — fasting, following a funeral, feeding the poor, and visiting the sick, all in one day.
tf.tf051.q: Whoever combines fasting, attending a funeral, feeding the poor, and visiting the sick in a single day will enter Jannah.
tf.tf051.x: This is the Abu Bakr Challenge in your Today tab — try to complete all four in one day!
tf.tf052.q: Whoever maintains family ties, Allah maintains ties with him.
tf.tf052.x: A message or a visit to reconnect kinship draws Allah's connection to you.
tf.tf053.q: Islam teaches that charity is best given publicly so others can see it.
tf.tf053.x: Hidden charity is praised — giving so secretly that the left hand does not know what the right hand gives.
tf.tf054.q: Feeding a poor person only counts if it is a full meal.
tf.tf054.x: Even a small meal or a single date counts with Allah.
tf.tf055.q: Laylatul Qadr is better than a thousand months.
tf.tf055.x: One night of worship outweighs over 83 years — a lifetime of deeds.
tf.tf056.q: Laylatul Qadr is guaranteed to fall on the 27th night every year.
tf.tf056.x: We are told to seek it in the ODD nights of the last ten — it could be any of them, so strive every night.
tf.tf057.q: We are instructed to seek Laylatul Qadr in the odd nights of the last ten days.
tf.tf057.x: Nights 21, 23, 25, 27, and 29 — this app highlights them for you.
tf.tf058.q: When the last ten days began, the Prophet ﷺ would tighten his waist belt and pray all night.
tf.tf058.x: He exerted himself in these nights more than at any other time — and woke his family too.
tf.tf059.q: The dua the Prophet ﷺ taught Aishah (RA) for Laylatul Qadr is: 'Allahumma innaka afuwwun tuhibbul afwa fafu anni.'
tf.tf059.x: 'O Allah, You are Pardoning and You love pardon, so pardon me.' Repeat it all night.
tf.tf060.q: The Prophet ﷺ observed I'tikaf only once in his life.
tf.tf060.x: He observed I'tikaf in the last ten days EVERY Ramadan — even partial i'tikaf carries reward.
tf.tf061.q: Standing in prayer on Laylatul Qadr with faith and hope of reward forgives past sins.
tf.tf061.x: One accepted night wipes the slate clean.
tf.tf062.q: The closest a servant is to Allah is while in sujood.
tf.tf062.x: Lengthen your sujood in the last ten nights and pour out your duas there.
tf.tf063.q: The three thirds of Ramadan are known as Mercy (Days 1-10), Forgiveness (Days 11-20), and Salvation (Days 21-30).
tf.tf063.x: You can compare your effort across all three in the Progress tab.
prep.intro.title: Ramadan Prep
guide.guide1.title: Daily Checklist
guide.guide1.body: You get 60+ daily deeds organised into 7 categories — Salah, Quran, Character, Charity, Avoidance, Abu Bakr Challenge, and Last 10 Nights. Tap any category to open it, then tick off what you've done. Your daily percentage updates as you go. Each category starts closed so you can focus on one area at a time.
guide.guide2.title: Quran Tracker
guide.guide2.body: Track your journey through all 604 pages of the Quran. After each reading session, tap "Log reading" and add your pages — they add up throughout the day. The dashboard shows your total progress, which Juz you're on, and how many pages per day you need to complete the Quran by Day 30. A chart shows your actual pace vs the ideal pace so you know if you're on track.
guide.guide3.title: Streaks
guide.guide3.body: The app tracks four consecutive-day streaks: Fajr at the Masjid, Isha at the Masjid, daily Quran, and giving Sadaqah. Each day you keep it up, your count grows. At milestones like 3, 7, 10, and 20 days, you'll see a congratulations message pop up. It's a simple way to build consistency in worship.
guide.guide4.title: 12 Badges
guide.guide4.body:
Unlock achievements as you progress through Ramadan:
First Step — do anything on Day 1
Week One — log all 7 days of the first week
Halfway — stay active for the first 15 days
Fajr Warrior — 7-day Fajr at Masjid streak
Tahajjud Master — pray Tahajjud on 7 nights
Quran Lover — read Quran on 15 days
Generous — give charity on 10 days
Abu Bakr — complete the full challenge in one day
Abu Bakr Gold — do it on 3 different days
Last 10 Hero — avg 70%+ across the Last 10 Nights
Perfectionist — hit 100% on 3 days
Champion — score 60%+ on 20 days

Print your PDF report on Eid and use the badges to celebrate and reward your kids!
guide.guide5.title: Last 10 Nights & Laylatul Qadr
guide.guide5.body: A countdown to the Last 10 Nights begins on Day 15. When Day 21 arrives, a bonus worship category unlocks with extra deeds like I'tikaf, long sujood, and extra Quran. Odd nights (21, 23, 25, 27, 29) are highlighted across the app to remind you — any one of them could be Laylatul Qadr.
guide.guide6.title: Abu Bakr Challenge
guide.guide6.body: The Prophet ﷺ once asked his companions four questions: "Who among you is fasting today? Who followed a funeral? Who fed someone? Who visited someone who is sick?" Abu Bakr (RA) was the only one who said "I did" to all four. This challenge asks you to do the same in a single day. When you've completed 3 out of 4, the app encourages you to go for all four.
guide.guide7.title: Sisters' Menstrual Cycle
guide.guide7.body: Activate the toggle on the Today tab during your cycle. Salah and fasting items will be greyed out and excluded from your percentage. This way, your score reflects only the deeds that apply to you — so you can still aim for 100%.
guide.guide8.title: Progress & Charts
guide.guide8.body: The Me tab gives you a full picture of your Ramadan: your average completion, a heatmap of all 30 days, a comparison of the three thirds of Ramadan (Mercy, Forgiveness, Salvation), a daily trend line, and a breakdown of your effort by category.
guide.guide9.title: Learn
guide.guide9.body: Test what you have learned. The Learn tab turns the hadith and ayat behind the deeds in this app into short quizzes: true-or-false cards in six categories (Fasting, Salah & Dhikr, Quran, Character, Charity and the Last 10 Nights), multiple-choice questions, and flashcards that come back when they are due for review. Every answer shows its source on sunnah.com or quran.com, and your accuracy and best scores are saved, so keep going until you master them all.
guide.guide10.title: Competition Mode
guide.guide10.body: Run a Ramadan competition for your school, university, mosque, company, family or community. Organisers create a competition with Top 10 prizes and get a 6-letter join code plus a printable QR poster. Participants enter the code (or tap a personal invitation link) and their daily deeds, points and Quran pages feed a live leaderboard — individuals and classes/teams. Organisers get a roster with inactivity and integrity flags, bulk enrolment, a daily points cap, CSV export, Eid certificates for everyone, and a child-privacy mode. Only a display name and scores are shared — never the checklist details.
guide.guide11.title: New to Islam or Learning?
guide.guide11.body: Every deed in the checklist has a hadith reference and a short explanation behind it. Turn on "Detail Mode" (in Me, under Settings) and you'll see the source and meaning of each item. You don't need any prior knowledge — the app teaches you as you use it.
guide.guide12.title: PDF Report
guide.guide12.body: Download a printable PDF of your entire Ramadan journey — your daily completion, Quran pages read, badges unlocked, and best streaks. It's a meaningful keepsake, and a great way to celebrate your children's achievements on Eid day.
guide.guide13.title: Privacy & Data
guide.guide13.body: By default everything stays on your device: deeds, Quran pages, badges, journal and settings are stored in this browser, and no account is needed. If you choose to create an account, a copy of your tracker data is kept so it can sync between your devices, and you can delete it at any time. In a competition only your display name, an optional class or team, and your total scores are shared — never which deeds you ticked. You can export a backup file at any time and import it on another device, and the app works offline.
